notes.meaning: Judah's leaders looked to Egypt for chariots and cavalry to defend them against Assyria instead of seeking the Lord. God had warned His people not to return to Egypt or put their trust in military might alone. By running to human allies for safety, they ignored the Holy One of Israel who had always protected them. We are reminded to turn to God first in our troubles rather than trusting in human strength.

God reminds Judah that He is far wiser than any foreign advisers or rulers. When He speaks and announces judgment, He never changes His mind or takes back His words. He will take action both against the unfaithful leaders in Judah and the Egyptian allies they run to for help.

Egypt is made up of mortal humans, not God, and their war horses are mere flesh without divine power. When the Lord acts in judgment, human strength cannot stand against Him. Both the Egyptian helpers and the people of Judah who leaned on them will fall together. True security comes only from relying on the Spirit of God.

The Lord describes Himself as a powerful lion growling over its food, completely unafraid of a crowd of shouting shepherds. In the same way, the Lord of Hosts will descend to protect Mount Zion, and no enemy army can frighten Him away. Even though Judah had been disobedient, God graciously promised to stand guard over His city.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars translate the phrase to say that God will come down to fight against Mount Zion in judgment, rather than fighting to defend it.

notes.meaning: God also compares Himself to a mother bird hovering over her nest to protect her young from harm. He will shield Jerusalem and rescue it from destruction with swift and tender care. The promise that He will pass over the city recalls how God spared His people during the first Passover in Egypt.

Isaiah urges the people of Israel to turn back to the God they had deeply betrayed. Even after walking far away into stubborn rebellion, the door of repentance is still open to them. God's amazing mercy invites broken sinners to return home and find forgiveness.

When the people truly return to God, they will throw away the useless gold and silver idols they made with their own hands. Real repentance always shows itself in outward action and a change of lifestyle. They will see that their false gods are completely powerless to save them.

The mighty Assyrian army will be destroyed, but not by human soldiers or ordinary weapons of war. God will send an angel with an unseen sword of judgment to strike down the invaders outside Jerusalem. The proud enemy will run away in terror, and their finest warriors will be defeated.

The king of Assyria will flee in panic to his stronghold in Nineveh, and his military officers will scatter at the Lord's battle standard. The Lord's presence lives in Zion like a burning fire and hearth. That holy fire brings warmth and protection to His people, but burns up the enemies who attack them.
